questions.q: What are the two variable namespaces every SSIS package has?
options: User and System
Local and Global
Package and Project
Public and Private
questions.explain: User is where your own variables land by default; System holds the fixed, predefined variables SSIS itself maintains, like PackageName and StartTime.

questions.q: What determines a variable's scope when you click Add Variable in the Variables window?
options: Whatever container, task, or the package design surface itself was selected right before you opened the Variables window and clicked Add Variable
The order variables appear in the grid
The variable's data type
Scope is fixed to the whole package for every variable, with no way to change it
questions.explain: Scope is set at creation time by whatever was selected on the design surface — a container, a task, or the package itself. To change it afterward, you select the variable and click Move Variable rather than editing a column directly.

questions.q: What happens when a variable's EvaluateAsExpression property is set to True?
options: The variable's value becomes the live result of an assigned expression instead of a fixed literal
The variable becomes read-only
The variable moves into the System namespace
The variable can no longer be used in an Execute SQL Task
questions.explain: With EvaluateAsExpression set to True, the variable stops holding a static literal and instead recalculates its value from the assigned expression every time it's evaluated — for example, DATEPART("mm", GETDATE()) to always hold the current month.

questions.q: Which of these can you NOT do to a system variable?
options: Add new ones or delete existing ones
Read its current value at run time
Use it inside a property expression
Toggle whether it raises an event when its value changes
questions.explain: System variables are predefined by SSIS — you can't add to or delete from the System namespace. The only configurable option on a system variable is RaiseChangedEvent.

questions.q: By default, which columns does the Variables window show without opening Grid Options?
options: Name, Scope, Data Type, and Value
Name, Namespace, Description, and Expression
Only Name and Value
Every property a variable has, all at once
questions.explain: Namespace, Raise Change Event, Description, and Expression are all hidden by default and only appear once you click Grid Options and select them.
